papers.title: The mitochondrial theory of sleep: an integrative framework for understanding sleep-wake regulation.
papers.summary: Proposes an integrative mitochondrial theory of sleep, synthesizing disease models, mechanistic data, and bioinformatics gene enrichment analysis. Identifies nine mitochondrial protein-coding genes enriched in oxidative phosphorylation, synaptic, and sleep pathways, and suggests sleep deprivation is linked to calcium signaling, mitochondrial gene expression, ROS, and ATP production, offering a testable model and therapeutic targets such as MCU1, CPT1A, and antioxidant regulators.

papers.title: Long-term monitoring reveals immobility-defined sleep fragmentation and behavioural alterations in collagen-induced arthritis mouse model of both sexes.
papers.summary: Long-term non-invasive monitoring of immobility-defined sleep in a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mouse model of both sexes revealed that during the rest phase, CIA mice had 50% less sleep time, shorter bouts, and more interruptions, along with reduced locomotor activity, impaired short-term memory, higher anxiety-like behavior, and altered social and exploratory behaviors. More frequent sleep interruptions were associated with higher arthritis scores, supporting long-term monitoring for studying sleep and behavioral alterations in experimental arthritis.

papers.title: Pregnancy Impacts Maternal Sleep: Focus on Kynurenine Pathway Activation in Female Rats
papers.summary: In pregnant and non-pregnant female rats, pregnancy increased dark-phase NREM and REM sleep and attenuated kynurenine-associated REM sleep disruption near parturition; salivary kynurenic acid distinguished kynurenine-fed females and correlated with brain levels.

papers.title: Chronic joint pain drives sex-specific changes in hippocampal glutamatergic signaling and sleep.
papers.summary: Using a monoiodoacetate knee pain mouse model, this study found sex-specific changes in hippocampal glutamatergic signaling and sleep architecture: both sexes developed mechanical hypersensitivity, but females exhibited poorer sleep outcomes. Injured males showed increased AMPAR-mediated excitatory activity, whereas injured females showed reduced NMDAR activity, and mechanical hypersensitivity correlated with reduced NMDAR/GluN2B function in females and altered AMPAR/NMDAR activity associated with REM sleep.

papers.title: Orexin receptor antagonists attenuate acute stress-induced disruptions in sleep states.
papers.summary: In adult male Sprague Dawley rats exposed to acute inescapable footshock stress, systemic administration of a dual orexin receptor antagonist (suvorexant), an OX1R-preferring antagonist (SB334867), and an OX2R-selective antagonist (EMPA) partially restored REM sleep and attenuated stress-induced increases in NREM sleep. Dual receptor blockade most effectively attenuated NREM increases and reductions in sleep-onset latency, supporting further investigation of DORAs for stress-related sleep disturbance.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics reveals cell-type-specific circadian rhythms and their disruption by acute misalignment in mouse aorta
papers.summary: This study performed single-cell RNA sequencing of mouse aorta under aligned and acutely misaligned light-dark cycles, identifying cell-type-specific circadian rhythms and their disruption by misalignment. They found hundreds of cycling genes in vascular smooth muscle cells and fibroblasts, with sex differences and molecular evidence of proteostatic stress after misalignment.

papers.title: Genetic ALS-Progressive Sleep Defects Precede the Onset of Clinical Disease.
papers.summary: In a longitudinal observational cohort of 18 presymptomatic ALS mutation carriers and 3 noncarrier relatives, polysomnography and EEG at baseline and follow-up (2.3 ± 1.5 years) showed that sleep macro- and microarchitectural alterations progressively worsened in all carriers. Progression appeared independent of proximity to motor onset, suggesting sleep measures as noninvasive surrogate biomarkers of premanifest ALS progression.

papers.title: An Investigation of Sleep Macro- and Microarchitecture by APOE Genotype.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 3,081 adults aged 50–85 from the Sleep Heart Health Study found that while sleep macroarchitecture was largely comparable across APOE genotypes, micro-level traits differed: ε4 homozygotes had lower spindle power and a dose-response decrease in spindle frequency, and both odds ratio product and arousal index decreased with each ε4 count. These microarchitectural alterations may contribute to Alzheimer's disease risk in ε4 carriers.

papers.title: Exercise timing as a potential temporal regulator of neurolymphatic physiology in neurodegenerative proteinopathies: a mechanistic framework.
papers.summary: This review proposes a mechanistic framework treating exercise timing as a temporal regulator of neurolymphatic clearance in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, linking timed exercise to glymphatic-meningeal lymphatic function, vascular pulsatility, circadian alignment, and sleep architecture. It argues that timed exercise is a testable biological perturbation rather than a proven disease-modifying treatment and calls for matched-dose trials integrating accelerometry, sleep physiology, circadian measures, vascular assessments, and protein biomarkers.

papers.title: Adaptive Forgetting for Nonstationary Optimization: Towards Robust EEG Decoding
papers.summary: The paper introduces AFOR, a tensor-wise adaptive optimizer with a Residual-Alignment Signal Scorer and Adaptive Forgetting Controller that dynamically estimates the second-moment decay coefficient for nonstationary cross-subject EEG decoding. Under a strict cross-subject protocol on three EEG benchmarks, AFOR achieved the best average performance among compared optimizers, improving mean test accuracy over Adam by 3.00%, 2.07%, and 4.38%.

papers.title: Quantum machine learning for detection of sleep deprivation from EEG signals
papers.summary: This study applied Quantum Support Vector Machines and Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks to classify sleep-deprived versus well-rested states from resting-state EEG using spectral band power, band ratios, Hjorth parameters, and functional connectivity features encoded into quantum states. The Hybrid Quantum Neural Network achieved accuracies of 96.88% at the epoch level and 81.25% at the subject level, outperforming previously reported results.

papers.title: Lifespan EEG reference charts disentangle alpha-band alterations in neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders
papers.summary: The authors generated lifespan brain reference charts for alpha peak frequency and power from raw and 1/f-adjusted EEG spectra in a large outpatient cohort (N=22,094; age 1-100) and applied them to inpatient mental disorder groups. They found alpha power consistently reduced across diagnostic groups, while alpha peak frequency showed a method-dependent dissociation: raw spectra suggested slowing but 1/f-adjusted estimates revealed acceleration, indicating aperiodic components can mask oscillatory changes.

papers.title: Electroencephalography as a biomarker of brain function in domestic ruminants: a systematic review and critical appraisal.
papers.summary: This systematic review evaluated EEG as a biomarker of brain function in domestic ruminants across 112 studies, examining consciousness, nociception, anesthesia, hypoxia-ischemia, neurodevelopment, and neurological disorders while critically appraising methodological limitations. It reports that EEG consistently reflects context-dependent cortical network alterations but its interpretation as a direct surrogate of consciousness or nociception remains limited due to substantial heterogeneity in acquisition, analysis, and interpretation.

papers.title: Running out the clock: Circadian rhythm dysfunction in cognitive disease.
papers.summary: This review examines circadian rhythm dysfunction in cognitive diseases, highlighting pathways such as clock genes, oxidative stress, and gut microbiota. It proposes that targeting these pathways could offer new strategies for cognitive disease treatment, though no specific clinical results are reported.

papers.title: Machine Learning Using Electroencephalography Predicts Acute Cerebral Injury in the Pediatric ICU.
papers.summary: A prospective study applied machine learning to clinical and EEG features to predict acute cerebral injury in pediatric ICU patients. The SVM with RBF kernel achieved the highest accuracy (AUROC 0.95, test accuracy 0.90) for binary classification, while logistic regression performed best for multiclass classification (accuracy 0.77).

papers.title: Sleep electroencephalography-derived brain health and long-term cognitive decline in community-dwelling adults.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: In 639 community-dwelling adults, higher sleep EEG-derived Brain Health Score (BHS) was associated with slower cognitive decline in memory, executive function, and language over an average of 14.3 years. Brain Age Index (BAI) showed no association with cognitive decline.

papers.title: Chronobiology of fracture repair: local molecular clocks, rhythm protection, and time-anchored translation.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on circadian regulation of fracture repair, noting that local molecular clocks operate in the fracture niche and that perioperative disruptions may affect healing. It advocates for a time-anchored research framework but concludes that current evidence does not support specific clinical chronotherapy recommendations.

papers.title: Melatonin, circadian metabolism, mitochondrial remodeling, and cell size dynamics in primitive hematopoietic stem cells.
papers.summary: This paper demonstrates that circadian cues coordinate mitochondrial remodeling, metabolic reprogramming, and structural adaptation in primitive hematopoietic stem cells, with nocturnal melatonin associated with enhanced long-term repopulating capacity and glycolytic reprogramming via systemic circadian inputs.

papers.title: EEG Microstate Alterations in Anhedonia Subtypes of Major Depressive Disorder and Their Modulation by Intermittent Theta-Burst Stimulation.
papers.summary: In 50 MDD patients stratified by anhedonia severity, iTBS modulated EEG microstate dynamics differently: low-anhedonia patients showed normalization of most microstate parameters, while high-anhedonia patients had persistent abnormalities. In high-anhedonia patients, clinical improvement correlated with microstate changes, suggesting microstates as treatment response markers.

papers.title: Adrenergic Pathways Mediate Circadian IOP Rhythm in Rats.
papers.summary: This study used wireless telemetry to monitor intraocular pressure (IOP) in rats and applied adrenergic receptor agonists and antagonists to identify mechanisms underlying circadian IOP rhythm. It found that β-, α1-, and α2-adrenergic pathways are all necessary to elevate IOP during subjective night, while β- and α1-receptor activation is sufficient to raise daytime IOP to nighttime levels.

papers.title: Vascular Bed Specificity in the Endothelial Link Between Sleep Deprivation and Hypertension.
papers.summary: This letter likely discusses vascular bed-specific endothelial mechanisms linking sleep deprivation to hypertension. No abstract was provided, so a detailed summary cannot be given.

papers.title: Nocturnal sleep abnormalities occur before motor function deterioration in early-treated patients with infantile-onset Pompe disease: a two-decade newborn screening cohort study.
papers.summary: In a two-decade cohort of early-treated infantile-onset Pompe disease patients, longitudinal polysomnography and spirometry revealed that nocturnal sleep abnormalities, particularly obstructive sleep apnea, emerged before motor function deterioration. Sleep apnea occurred in 11 of 16 patients at a median age of 7.8 years, often with relatively preserved motor and respiratory function.

papers.title: Postoperative Sleep Disturbance and Functional Recovery Following Hip Fracture Surgery: A 13-Month Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.
papers.summary: This 13-month prospective cohort of 323 hip fracture surgery patients characterized postoperative sleep disturbance (PSD) and its association with functional recovery. PSD prevalence decreased from 88.2% at 1 month to 27.8% at 13 months, and worse sleep quality was independently associated with lower functional status; male sex and higher preoperative comorbidity burden were risk factors for slower recovery.

papers.title: Application of Circadian Rhythm-Based Pulmonary Rehabilitation in Patients with Severe Pneumonia-A Feasibility Study With Convenience Sampling.
papers.journal: Archives of rehabilitation research and clinical translation
papers.summary: This feasibility study with convenience sampling assigned 93 severe pneumonia patients to routine pulmonary rehabilitation or a circadian rhythm-based comprehensive program. The intervention group had significantly shorter mechanical ventilation and hospital stay, higher rehabilitation compliance, better pulmonary function and sleep quality, and greater nursing satisfaction.

papers.title: Electroencephalography-functional magnetic resonance imaging using a familial temporal lobe epilepsy model in cats: an exploratory methodological pilot study.
papers.summary: This exploratory methodological pilot study developed and evaluated simultaneous EEG-fMRI in cats with familial spontaneous epilepsy. While BOLD activation was detected in all sessions at an exploratory threshold, no activation survived multiple comparison correction, and individual-level epileptogenic zone localization remains insufficient for clinical use.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Monitoring for Seizure Risk Stratification in the Critically III.
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of continuous EEG (cEEG) for seizure risk stratification in critically ill patients, highlighting the 2HELPS2B score as a validated tool to guide monitoring duration and optimize cEEG resource use.

papers.title: Multimodal neuroimaging in schizophrenia: a systematic review of EEG and fMRI integration.
papers.summary: This systematic review evaluated 16 simultaneous EEG-fMRI studies in schizophrenia to assess neurovascular coupling and network abnormalities. It reported consistent EEG findings (e.g., impaired P50 suppression, reduced P300, gamma/beta dysregulation) and fMRI findings (e.g., default mode network alterations), suggesting possible neurovascular decoupling but emphasizing methodological heterogeneity and hypothesis-generating results.

papers.title: Sleep Duration and Sun Exposure in Portuguese Children: Associations With Obesity Indicators.
papers.journal: American journal of human biology : the official journal of the Human Biology Council
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 4755 Portuguese children aged 3-10, associations between sun exposure and sleep duration were examined with sex-stratified multiple linear regression. Modest sex-specific associations were found: in partially adjusted models, sun exposure was positively associated with sleep duration in girls and negatively in boys, but in fully adjusted models only a negative association for boys on Sundays remained (β=-4.57, 95% CI: -8.22 to -0.91).

papers.title: Inter-rater reliability in drug-induced sleep endoscopy: experience-driven interpretation, decision-making, and the emerging role of artificial intelligence.
papers.summary: Inter-rater reliability of drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) interpretation using the VOTE classification was evaluated among 12 human raters and an AI model on 20 recordings, showing moderate agreement (weighted kappa 0.255–0.425 for obstruction grading; Fleiss' kappa 0.287–0.370 for collapse pattern) and higher agreement for senior than junior raters. AI performance was lower than expert consensus, especially for therapeutic decision-making.

papers.title: Illuminating Risk: An Ecological Analysis of Artificial Light at Night and Childhood Myopia Using State-Level US Data.
papers.summary: This ecological analysis of 2019 data from 46 US states used generalized additive modeling to examine the association between artificial light at night (ALAN) and childhood myopia prevalence. Higher ALAN was significantly associated with higher myopia prevalence (F=8.39, p=0.0068), with the final model explaining 65.3% of deviance; screen time showed a nonlinear relationship, and Medicaid coverage had a U-shaped association.

papers.title: Circadian biology and sexual offending: A hypothesis integrating chronobiological rhythms with Routine Activity Theory.
papers.summary: This hypothesis paper integrates chronobiological principles with Routine Activity Theory to propose a multilevel framework in which biological timing may act as a background modulator of neurobehavioral state, while social routines and environmental exposure determine offending opportunity. It emphasizes that temporal patterns in sexual offending do not imply causation and proposes a Chronobiology-Routine Activity Interaction Model requiring prospective research.

papers.title: Sleep duration inversely correlates with glucolipid metabolism in patients with new-onset type 2 diabetes mellitus.
papers.summary: In 168 patients with new-onset type 2 diabetes mellitus, sleep duration was inversely correlated with glucolipid metabolism indices and abdominal total fat area, and positively correlated with good glycemic control. Short sleep duration, along with high BMI, FBG, TG, and TFA, was identified as an independent contributor to poor glycemic control.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnoea and glucose dysregulation in type 2 diabetes: a systematic review of the literature.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-based systematic review of 11 studies found that obstructive sleep apnoea was consistently associated with poorer glycemic control, increased insulin resistance, and adverse metabolic profiles in individuals with type 2 diabetes, with some evidence for severity-dependent effects and potential metabolic benefits of CPAP therapy.

papers.title: Effect of modernized collaborative care for depression on individual depressive symptoms: A secondary analysis of the eIMPACT trial.
papers.summary: Secondary analysis of the eIMPACT randomized controlled trial (216 primary care patients) found that modernized collaborative care (internet/telephonic CBT and/or antidepressants) improved 15 of 20 SCL-20 items and 7 of 9 PHQ-9 items compared to usual care, with moderate-to-large effects on most symptoms but no significant advantage for suicidality, loneliness, sexual dysfunction, appetite change, or psychomotor symptoms.

papers.title: Preoperative Anxiety and Early Postoperative Recovery Among Women Undergoing Gynecologic Surgery in Vietnam: A Prospective Longitudinal Observational Study.
papers.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
papers.summary: In a prospective longitudinal observational study of 394 women undergoing gynecologic surgery in Vietnam, 33.2% screened positive for preoperative anxiety, which was associated with greater early postoperative pain and higher insomnia severity scores, but not with early functional status.

papers.title: The Global Initiative for Obstructive Sleep Apnea (GIFOSA): Rationale, Strategic Framework, and Call to Action.
papers.summary: This paper presents the rationale and strategic framework of the Global Initiative for Obstructive Sleep Apnea (GIFOSA), an implementation-focused initiative to address global disparities in obstructive sleep apnea care through coordinated clinical, workforce, person-centered, and policy pillars.

papers.title: Key elements of left ventricular assist device adjustment: A qualitative exploratory study.
papers.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
papers.summary: This qualitative study of 20 left ventricular assist device (LVAD) recipients identified key elements of adjustment including physical ability, caregiver dependence, self-care, roles, public perception, and emotional connection, highlighting the importance of connection, role restoration, and public perception in LVAD-supported life.

papers.title: Associations of exercise frequency, exercise session duration, and sleep duration with depressive symptoms among Chinese adolescents: a complex-survey cross-sectional analysis of CFPS2022.
papers.journal: Frontiers in sports and active living
papers.summary: In a complex-survey cross-sectional analysis of 2,861 Chinese adolescents from CFPS2022, exercise frequency and sleep duration were modestly associated with depressive symptoms, whereas exercise session duration showed no clear association. The largest adjusted difference was for once-daily exercise vs. never exercising (B = -1.08), and sleep duration was nonlinearly associated with CES-D8 scores (higher scores at 6 and 7 hours relative to 8 hours).

papers.title: Early Postoperative Predictors of Two-Year Satisfaction after Ream and Run Arthroplasty.
papers.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
papers.summary: In 375 patients who underwent ream-and-run arthroplasty with minimum 2-year follow-up, early postoperative shoulder comfort at rest (SST-1) at 3 months and comfort during sleep (SST-2) at 6 months were independent predictors of 2-year satisfaction. Positive SST-1 at 3 months was associated with 15.7 times increased odds of satisfaction, and positive SST-2 at 6 months with 6.2 times increased odds.

papers.title: Assisted cycling in non-ambulant adults with cerebral palsy: exploratory effects and feasibility in residential care.
papers.summary: This 10-week controlled feasibility study of assisted cycling in 14 non-ambulant adults with cerebral palsy (GMFCS III-V) found that the intervention was feasible and generally well tolerated, with median attendance of 24/30 sessions. No significant group-level changes were observed, but individual improvements in pain, constipation, and power output were seen in some participants, and two experienced moderate adverse events.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
